support.text:
# Authored comparison, not an execution result

The central comparison is A-complete versus B-duplicate under the exact same
review.json. It tests whether plausible counts, agreeing ordinary operands and
a firing control establish reviewed-measurement coverage. The predicted answer
for this construction is no: the supplied verifier should distinguish the pair
through missing and duplicate reviewed measurement identities.

The fixture was authored for this question. Its parcel-check ordinary case has
three reviewed measurements: seal, label and route. Its switch-control case has
one reviewed measurement, switch. This is hypothetical review input, not an
actual release, managerial admission or evidence of source authenticity. All
six case fields and the four review fields meet the supplied validator's
written constraints by inspection. The review uses no repeated JSON keys.

A has ten valid ledger rows: six declaration/reach/admission rows, three ordinary
comparisons and one control comparison. B changes only the measurement string
on line 5 from label to seal. Every operand, mismatch flag, note, declaration,
control row and event position stays fixed. Thus each still has three raw
ordinary comparison rows with agreeing operands and one raw control comparison
whose operands differ. B presents seal twice, omits label and presents route
once. Neither the declarations nor the authored review grant this substitution.

The third ordinary measurement is intentional. The verifier should count route
in B while excluding both ambiguous seal comparisons. Its ordinary compared
count should therefore be 1, avoiding a generic zero-ordinary-comparisons
explanation. A should count all three. Both should count the same firing control.
The summary's count changes as an outcome of membership checking; it cannot be
held fixed together with this change in duplicate membership. The input row
count, ordinary agreement and control remain fixed.

The complete proposed observation is the tuple of parse problems, full summary
with explicit review cases, and prerequisites. Parse problems must not be
discarded merely because prerequisites is empty. Raw-ledger parse_rows uses
ordinary JSON decoding; the control review must use loads_control, which
rejects repeated keys. These specimen bytes have no repeated keys, so the
central distinction does not depend on that decoder difference.

Secondary probes are separate from the central pair:

- C changes only the ordinary label row's note. Its full summary and
  prerequisites should equal A's, with no parse problems.
- D changes only the control row's actual operand from true to false, keeping
  the claimed mismatch true. Operand recomputation should extinguish the
  control and report the contradictory flag. A versus D makes the firing
  control operand-sensitive rather than merely a child-provided claim.
- E swaps the ordinary reach and admission rows. Membership labels and operands
  remain A's, but the admission has no prior reach. It should expose the event
  sequence requirement separately from the central membership effect.
- F appends one malformed line after A. It should retain A's full summary and
  empty prerequisites while separately reporting a parse problem at line 11.
  This prevents an empty-prerequisites-only observation from concealing a gap.

No project module, proposed observer, experiment, test or submission helper was
executed during construction. The six specimens are six proposed evaluations,
not six trials. Supplied tests were read as examples of source assertions; these
case IDs, three-measurement fixture, operands and exact specimens were authored
independently. No historical study answers were consulted.

Protected state consists of the pinned ledger, control decoder and supplied
tests; the common review; the proposed observer; and the selected specimens and
predictions whose stability the future comparison relies on. The author has
written only assigned output paths and promises no changes to those inputs.
AUTHORED-IDENTITIES.json records point-in-time author observations of their
bytes. These observations are neither coordinator-witnessed identity checks nor
continuous-preservation evidence. Root independently holds source pins and a
witness, but this author has not inspected either. Any future execution needs
its own authorized environment, independent preservation witness and retained
stdout/stderr/status. Before/after hashes cannot prove continuous preservation.

The provided observer is a proposal for the maintainer's next decision. It
loads only explicitly named packet files after checking their pinned hashes,
decodes the review with the supplied control decoder, and emits each specimen's
full observation. It deliberately does not implement a second ledger verifier
or assert the predicted answer. It does not invoke the wrapper review validator;
the review constraints still require the maintainer's inspection. The full
wrapper, custody, release authenticity, program exit semantics, and truth of the
child's operands remain outside the question.

From the repository root, the proposed command is:

```sh
/usr/bin/python3 -I -B coordination/fresh-authoring-01/author/attempt-01/support/observe-proposed.py --packet .scratch/fresh-authoring-01/subject-01 --specimens coordination/fresh-authoring-01/author/attempt-01/support
```

This command has not run and is not authorized by this document. It proposes
Python 3.10 or newer at that exact interpreter path, standard library only,
read access to the specified immutable files, no project installation and no
bytecode writes. Interpreter version/availability has not been checked. The
maintainer must first designate fresh retained stdout/stderr/status destinations
and the independent witness and decide whether this observer and environment
are adequate. An import, decoding, preservation or tool failure ends that
proposed execution; retain partial output rather than modifying an input and
continuing. This is an inspectable command proposal, not a reproducibility
guarantee or permission to run.

If the predictions hold, they distinguish the two explanations for these
specimens. They do not establish universal ledger completeness, the sufficiency
of mechanical prerequisites for scientific validity, or the truth or
independence of review and operands. No bypass or unexpected execution finding
is claimed. A mismatch between prediction and later observation is a result to
inspect, not something to erase by tuning the specimen.

# Source-derived predictions; no observations from execution

All A–F use the same exact review.json. In the table, comparisons and mismatches
mean the verifier's counted values, not raw compare-row totals. Each valid
specimen has four raw compare rows: three ordinary and one control.

| Specimen | Parsed valid rows | Parse problems | Ordinary compared / mismatches | Control compared / mismatches |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| A-complete | 10 | empty | 3 / 0 | 1 / 1 |
| B-duplicate | 10 | empty | 1 / 0 | 1 / 1 |
| C-note-invariant | 10 | empty | 3 / 0 | 1 / 1 |
| D-control-extinguished | 10 | empty | 3 / 0 | 1 / 0 |
| E-admission-before-reach | 10 | empty | 0 / 0 | 1 / 1 |
| F-parse-problem | 10 | line 11, invalid JSON row | 3 / 0 | 1 / 1 |

For A, B, C, D and F, each population has declared=1, reached=1,
admitted=1, refused=0. For E, ordinary admitted=0 while ordinary declared=1,
reached=1 and refused=0; control is unchanged. The expected ordinary
mismatching_cases list is empty in every specimen. The control list is
["switch-control"] except D, where it is empty.

A, C and F should have empty arrays in every summary diagnostic field and
prerequisites=[]; F additionally has its separate parse problem. For B the only
nonempty summary diagnostic fields should be:

```json
{
  "missing_measurements": [{"case":"parcel-check","measurement":"label"}],
  "duplicate_measurements": [{"case":"parcel-check","measurement":"seal"}]
}
```

B's prerequisites, in source order, should be exactly:

```json
[
  "missing measurements: parcel-check:label",
  "duplicate measurements: parcel-check:seal"
]
```

D should have inconsistent_comparisons=["switch-control"], with all other
summary diagnostics empty. Its prerequisites should be exactly:

```json
[
  "no control produced a nonzero disagreement; the instrument was not observed to fire",
  "mismatch flags contradict recorded operands for: switch-control"
]
```

E's nonempty summary diagnostic fields should be:

```json
{
  "compared_without_admission": ["parcel-check"],
  "sequence_problems": ["parcel-check: admission requires prior reach and cannot repeat"],
  "unresolved_admission": ["parcel-check"]
}
```

E's prerequisites, in source order, should be exactly:

```json
[
  "no ordinary comparison was recorded",
  "comparisons recorded while cases were not admitted: parcel-check",
  "cases without an admission outcome: parcel-check",
  "parcel-check: admission requires prior reach and cannot repeat"
]
```

In E, missing_measurements and uncompared should remain empty because the
ordinary case never acquired an accepted true admission. That absence must not
be interpreted as coverage. Its admission and sequence diagnostics carry the
gap instead. In F, malformed_rows should remain empty because parse_rows
filters the invalid line out before summarize sees it; parse problems carry
that gap. The exact JSON decoder error wording is not predicted.

These predictions follow the supplied source's set reconciliation, exclusion
of every duplicate occurrence from counts, operand recomputation and event
state transitions. They are hypotheses awaiting a separately commissioned
execution. Structural acceptance by the submission helper would not verify any
table entry or conclusion.

"""UNEXECUTED proposal: emit observations, never an experiment verdict.

Future execution requires a separate grant and independent output capture.
No project installation, sys.path mutation, wrapper operation or subprocess.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys


PINNED = {
    "ledger.py": "e77d83e723d28385b73370832d6a2b0f2f87fcc84c6ad2905135d68eb0ee9696",
    "_json.py": "794f886883bab334582a4b16e9d60137498c2e7c2f3de259b0ce9680a05ada92",
    "test_stewart_ledger.py": "332e4a1ad8cd409b520ca7d11242ee7f2779e7aed5bbf0ab3376232c810c01ce",
}
SPECIMENS = (
    "A-complete.jsonl",
    "B-duplicate.jsonl",
    "C-note-invariant.jsonl",
    "D-control-extinguished.jsonl",
    "E-admission-before-reach.jsonl",
    "F-parse-problem.jsonl",
)


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def emit(value):
    print(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False), flush=True)


def load_selected(name, path):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--packet", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--specimens", required=True, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    paths = {"packet/" + name: args.packet / name for name in PINNED}
    paths.update({"authored/" + name: args.specimens / name for name in (
        "review.json", "PREDICTIONS.md", "CONSTRUCTION.md", *SPECIMENS
    )})
    paths["observer"] = Path(__file__)
    before = {name: digest(path) for name, path in paths.items()}
    emit({"stage": "before", "python": sys.version, "executable": sys.executable,
          "hashes": before, "continuous_preservation_established": False})
    for name, expected in PINNED.items():
        if before["packet/" + name] != expected:
            raise RuntimeError("Pinned input differs; stop before loading: " + name)
    ledger = load_selected("selected_ledger", args.packet / "ledger.py")
    decoder = load_selected("selected_control_json", args.packet / "_json.py")
    review = decoder.loads_control((args.specimens / "review.json").read_bytes())
    # The supplied validator constraints require prior maintainer inspection.
    # This observer does not call or replace the wrapper review validator.
    for name in SPECIMENS:
        raw = (args.specimens / name).read_bytes()
        rows, problems = ledger.parse_rows(raw)
        summary = ledger.summarize(rows, cases=review["cases"])
        emit({"stage": "specimen", "name": name,
              "sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(), "bytes": len(raw),
              "parsed_rows": len(rows),
              "raw_valid_compare_rows": sum(row["kind"] == "compare" for row in rows),
              "parse_problems": problems, "summary": summary,
              "prerequisites": ledger.prerequisites(summary)})
    after = {name: digest(path) for name, path in paths.items()}
    emit({"stage": "after", "hashes": after, "same_at_endpoints": before == after,
          "continuous_preservation_established": False})
    if before != after:
        raise RuntimeError("Protected bytes differ at endpoints; retain output and stop")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Final self-check and revision account

I inspected the exact review and all six specimens selected in the accepted
draft SNAPSHOT.json, then reread my saved predictions and proposed observer as
text. I did not execute the ledger, observer, tests, helper or any trial.

No substantive change to the construction or predictions is warranted by this
self-check. The final envelope preserves every original support object and
adds this account, a final return, a cumulative final read ledger and the small
structural-result records described below. The original draft envelope, note,
read ledger, support files and assembly record remain preserved. In particular,
final/READS.json is a new path so that the completed draft READS.json is not
overwritten.

The exact selected specimens express the claimed distinctions:

| Claim | Selected text inspected |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen independent fixture | review.json lists parcel-check measurements seal, label and route once each, with expected_admission=true; switch-control independently lists switch. Declarations reproduce the fixture's fields. The review is authored hypothetical input, not an actual release. |
| Membership-only central variation | A and B each have ten rows. In B, line 5 says measurement=seal where A says label. Lines 4 and 5 therefore both name seal; line 6 still names route. The expected/actual operands remain equal within each ordinary row. |
| Ambiguity is present, not another ordinary mismatch | B's first seal row compares closed with closed; its second seal row compares the same route/batch object with itself. Their differing operand shapes do not make either row an operand disagreement. The duplicate identity is the source of the predicted exclusion of both rows. |
| Control and event scaffolding stay fixed in the pair | In A and B, ordinary declaration/reach/admission precede all three ordinary comparisons. Control declaration/reach/admission precede line 10, which compares false with true and claims mismatch=true. |
| Permitted invariance | C changes the label row's note only. Its membership, operands and event order remain A's. |
| Operand-sensitive control | D's control expected and actual operands are both false while mismatch remains true. The prediction explicitly includes both recomputed zero control mismatches and an inconsistent-comparisons diagnostic. |
| Sequence is a separate requirement | E places admission before reach for parcel-check. There is no second admission after reach. Its unchanged measurement labels therefore cannot imply accepted admission or coverage. |
| Parsing is a separate observation | F preserves A's ten rows and appends the literal line not a JSON row. The predicted line-11 parse problem is not claimed to become summarize's malformed_rows or prerequisites. |

The surviving route row in B supports the intended comparison: the predicted
refusal is not explained by an absence of all ordinary comparisons. The
verifier's counted ordinary comparison total changes from 3 to 1 as the
predicted consequence of duplicate exclusion. The promised constant is the raw
comparison-row count, not the verifier's post-membership count.

The observer text calls parse_rows, summarize with review["cases"], and
prerequisites separately, and emits the parse problems alongside the full
summary and prerequisites. It emits observations rather than asserting my
predictions. Its source checks and endpoint hashes remain a proposal, not
continuous-preservation evidence. Its control decoding is distinct from raw
ledger decoding; it does not purport to run the wrapper's review validator.

The saved helper stdout and ACCEPTED record report structural acceptance and
intellectual_assessment=not_performed. Root's RESULT reports exit 0 and five
successful byte/snapshot checks. I read those reports; I did not inspect root's
witness or repeat its checks. The final envelope selects the helper stdout and
root RESULT as attributed records, not as scientific verification. The final
envelope itself has not yet been submitted.

No unexpected substantive finding arose. This was a prompted inspection of
already authored text, not an execution or discovery of a bypass. The outcome
remains a construction with source-derived predictions that a maintainer can
inspect before deciding whether to commission the proposed six evaluations.
No cap or interface restriction required a changed conclusion or omitted
specimen. No failed final assembly has occurred as of this account.

scaffolding fixed. The predicted verifier response names missing label and
